title: codewalk: an interactive guide to the player

operator.task: Show a first-time listener the player page and let them try each control.
operator.guidance: Short phrases; after each try-it phrase the walk waits (pauseAfter) until the listener presses Space.

author: Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) for the author, 2026-11-14

phrases.text: Welcome to codewalk. This short guide shows you the page you are looking at, and asks you to try each control. After each try it waits for you.
At the top is the caption: the phrase you are hearing now.
This is the schema card. The parts of a schema that a phrase names are framed, like the ones on this page plan.
When a phrase points at code, the code card shows those lines. If the walk was started with dash dash ide and IntelliJ IDEA is open, it follows the code.
On the left, or in a drawer on a narrow window, is the contents panel. Press T to open or close it. The walk now waits: try T, then press Space to go on.
Space plays and pauses. The left and right arrows go one phrase back or forward.
The square brackets go one topic back or forward; with Shift, the arrows go one chapter.
Try it: press the left arrow. You hear the last phrase again, then this one, and the walk waits here. Then press Space.
In the contents panel, a click on any phrase jumps to it. The panel also shows where you are.
Z zooms the schema to the framed parts, and X opens it full size; Escape closes it. Try Z now, then press Space.
Press Q to type a question about what you just heard. The walk pauses, and the answer is shown; with Azure consent, it is also spoken.
The page shows who will answer: a short Claude call if it is installed and you consent, a coding session that is listening, or nobody.
With Azure consent, hold the microphone button to speak instead of typing. Ask something now, or press Space to go on.
An answer can be stopped at any time with Space, Escape, or the Stop answer button, which replaces Play during an answer. The walk then returns to where it was.
When something is wrong or unclear, press D. Write or say a note; the walk stops and keeps your place.
A coding session that listens gets your note at once. You agree a change, and the session amends the walk into a new version. Nothing is overwritten.
The new version is checked, loaded, and your place is mapped onto it. The walk continues where you stopped; changed phrases are played again.
New walks begin with a creation prompt. This repository has one in prompts, create walk. Give it to your coding agent together with the project you want explained.
That is the guide. To watch a real walk in view mode, run bootstrap dot py run demo; for the design of codewalk itself, run design.
